co_nappy_dugout_the.blurb: A limestone sport wall tucked into Rifle Mountain Park, the canyon cliff zone north of the town of Rifle on the Western Slope. It holds about two dozen bolted lines and nothing else: no trad, no bouldering. The difficulty sits firmly in the harder half of the scale, with a handful of 5.10s, then a thick middle of 5.12 and 5.13 and a couple of routes at 5.14. That makes it a better stop for climbers already working through the 5.12 range than for anyone looking for warm-ups. Quality is generally high, with several lines drawing three or four stars, and the climbing is the steep, technical limestone that put Rifle on the map. Pair it with the neighboring walls in the park for a fuller day.

co_left_side_2.blurb: The left-hand section of the Plotinus Wall, a granite face in Lower Dream Canyon, a side drainage off Boulder Canyon west of Boulder. It is the busiest of the wall's three sections, with roughly two dozen routes. Most are bolted, with a smaller handful of trad lines, and the rock offers slabs, corners, a dihedral and the odd crack. The grades run from about 5.8 to 5.13, but the bulk of the climbs fall at 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits climbers comfortable on steady mid-grade sport. Bolted pitches commonly carry seven to a dozen clips, so bring a full-length rope and a generous set of quickdraws.

co_solar_dome_aka_lighthouse_the.blurb: A small granite sport crag in Boulder Canyon, perched on a hilltop at about 7,600 feet. It looks unremarkable from below but is well equipped, with around two dozen bolted routes, most of them shorter than 70 feet. The grades lean toward the harder end of moderate: mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with a few easier lines in the 5.6 to 5.8 bracket for warming up. Because it sits on top of a rise, it catches sun for much of the day, which makes it pleasant when the canyon is cool but hot in midsummer, and it is also exposed to weather moving up the canyon. The walk in is longer than at most canyon crags, so plan on a proper hike.
